Negated findings and composite phenotype mentions are also annotated. Corpus construction combines automated pre-annotation, large language model (LLM)-assisted verification, and manual review and adjudication. Benchmarks cover entity recognition and normalization and patient-phenotype association extraction using gold-standard and predicted entities. The overall document-level entity F1 was 86.95%, while phenotype F1 was 79.33%. The best relation extraction macro-F1 decreased from 84.14% with gold-standard entities to 54.98% with predicted entities, highlighting the combined challenges of phenotype extraction and patient attribution. PatientPheX provides a resource for developing and evaluating patient-centered information extraction methods and supports the construction of structured patient-level knowledge resources for phenotype-driven biomedical research.

items.title: Synaptic microRNA dysregulation orchestrates aberrant glutamatergic transmission in a human neuronal model of 22q11.2 deletion syndrome
items.abstract_or_text: 22q11.2 Deletion Syndrome (22q11DS), the most prevalent chromosomal microdeletion disorder in humans (incidence ~1 in 4,000 live births), arises from hemizygous deletions of a 1.5-3.0 Mb region on chromosome 22. Notably, 20-30% of individuals with 22q11DS develop schizophrenia (SCZ) by early adulthood, making 22q11DS one of the strongest genetic risk factors for SCZ. However, the mechanisms by which the 22q11.2 deletion perturbs neuronal function and drive psychotic manifestations in 22q11DS remain poorly defined. In this study, we generated human 2D cortical neurons and 3D cortical organoids from induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) derived from clinically well-characterized individuals with 22q11DS. Cellular and electrophysiological analyses revealed that 22q11DS neurons exhibit hyperexcitability, reduced glutamatergic synaptic transmission, and impaired homeostatic synaptic plasticity, which are pathophysiological hallmarks that may be relevant to the clinical, cognitive, and psychophysiological profiles of patients. Transcriptomic profiling of neurons and synaptosomes from 22q11DS cortical organoids uncovered dysregulated immune pathways and synaptic gene networks. Integrative mRNA-microRNA network analysis identified synergistic downregulation of hsa-miR-185-5p and hsa-miR-128-3p at synapses, driving aberrant regulation of immune and synaptic transcripts. Experimental knockdown of these microRNAs in control neurons recapitulated the molecular and functional phenotypes of 22q11DS neurons, thereby establishing a mechanistic link to synaptic dysfunction and impaired plasticity. Collectively, these findings delineate a multimodal mechanistic framework that bridges genetic vulnerability, synaptic pathology, and psychosis penetrance in 22q11DS, positioning dysregulated synaptic microRNAs as nodal regulators of neurodevelopmental networks and potential therapeutic targets.

items.title: Dual-graph deconvolution of enzyme fitness: an interpretable framework to identify and explain catalytic modulators
items.abstract_or_text: Models trained on protein sequences can predict mutational effects, but their outputs represent a convolution of different phenotypes. Isolating stability-independent activity effects is essential for rational enzyme design, allosteric drug design and functional annotation, yet existing pLM-based deconvolution methods lack interpretability. Here, we introduce a hybrid framework that pairs stability predictors with probabilistic graphical models of coevolution. Benchmarked on all enzymes with available multidimensional deep mutational scanning data, our framework isolates stability-independent activity effects with a fidelity that matches analogous pLM-based approaches. Crucially, we reveal biophysically plausible communication pathways that align with previous knowledge and that we validate with experimental data across a diverse set of targets. This hybrid approach merges statistical and geometric deep learning into a zero-shot, explainable tool for targeted engineering and mechanistic discovery.

items.title: D3Seg: Dependency-Aware Diffusion for Brain Tumor Segmentation with Missing Modalities
items.abstract_or_text: Abstract Accurate brain tumor segmentation using multi-parametric MRI is critical for effective treatment planning. However, in clinical settings, complete acquisition of all MRI sequences is not always possible. The absence of certain MRI modalities results in substantial performance degradation in existing segmentation methods, which typically rely on naive feature concatenation or direct fusion strategies. To address this limitation, we propose a novel segmentation model D 3 Seg which is designed to maintain stable performance under missing-modality settings. D 3 Seg introduces Multi-hop Modality Graph Fusion (MMGF) to model higher-order inter-modality dependencies, a lightweight diffusion-based imputation mechanism to compensate for missing T1ce and FLAIR feature representations in latent space, and probability-space decision refinement to mitigate dominant-class overconfidence and improve delineation of underrepresented tumor subregions. We evaluate the proposed D 3 Seg model on BraTS 2023 Glioma as the primary benchmark and further test it on a subset of the external BraTS 2023 Meningioma cohort to assess generalization across tumor pathologies.The results are compared with the state-of-the-art models under different missing-modality conditions. The proposed model achieves approximately 1.5–2.0% Dice improvement on enhancing tumor (ET) and around 1.0% on tumor core (TC) across multiple missing-modality configurations compared to the current state-of-the-art model on BraTS Glioma dataset. Cross-cohort evaluation on BraTS Meningioma dataset demonstrates the generalizability of the proposed model, showing consistent improvements in the challenging TC and ET regions, with approximately 1.5-3.0% and 1.5-6.5% gains respectively across several missing-modality configurations.

items.title: Generative design of functional disordered regions in a developmental transcription factor
items.abstract_or_text: Rapid advances in protein structure design have not translated to intrinsically disordered regions (IDRs). This is largely due to our incomplete understanding of how IDR sequence encodes function. Here, we use stem cell differentiation as a model to map functional sequence features in the IDR of transcription factor RUNX2. We show that RUNX2 requires its C-terminal IDR to bind chromatin and regulate gene expression during osteogenesis. Surprisingly, linear IDR sequence is dispensable, and instead features of the conformational ensemble predict function. We develop an algorithm for rational IDR design based on biophysical principles, and use it to generate functional IDRs de novo. Together, these results illustrate the central role for TF IDRs in chromatin binding and extend generative protein design beyond the folded proteome.

items.title: An Imaging Risk Score for Bipolar Disorder: Multimodal Comparison and Integration with Polygenic Risk
items.abstract_or_text: Background: Biological risk scores provide objective markers of bipolar disorder (BD) liability. Large-scale genome-wide association studies (GWASs) have led to polygenic risk scores (PRSs) that capture genetic liability to BD at the individual level. We lack a comparable large-scale effort to leverage a brain-wide association study (BWAS) to create an imaging risk score (IRS) that captures brain structural liability to BD at the individual-level. Here, we conduct the largest multivariate BWAS of BD and develop a BD IRS. We compare the BD IRS to the PRS and assess their combined predictive performance in multimodal risk score (MRS) models. Methods: Our multivariate BD BWAS used 153 structural neuroimaging features from 3902 cases and 6855 controls (mean age (sd)=35.47 years (13.42), 56.70% female) in a cross-validated machine learning approach. Using the resulting model coefficients, we constructed an IRS. We then evaluated the out-of-sample performance of the IRS, PRS derived from the largest GWAS to date, and combined MRS model using logistic regression in a subset of individuals with imaging and genetic data (nBD=486, ncontrols=1701, age (sd)=33.10 (12.02), 56.47% female). We also performed stratified analyses for demographic and BD clinical groups. Prediction performance was quantified using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). Subsequent analyses examined associations between each risk score and BD relevant symptoms in developing youth. Outcomes: In predicting case status, the BD BWAS model achieved a mean AUCBD of 0.62 (sdBD=0.08) and in stratified analyses, had higher prediction than subgroup-specific BWAS models. The BD type II BWAS was the only exception (AUCBDII=0.60, sdBDII=0.07 vs AUCBD=0.58, sdBD=0.09). The BD PRS had an AUCBD of 0.65 (CI95%=0.63-0.68) and a higher AUC than subtype-specific PRS in stratified analyses. The PRS typically attained a higher AUC than the IRS. Notably, the IRS and PRS were uncorrelated (r=0.03, p=0.11). MRS models outperformed the prediction of individual PRS and IRS with the strongest prediction for BD type I (AUCBD=0.74, CI95%=0.70-0.78). The IRS had the strongest associations with BD-related symptoms in developing youth including increased energy (OR=1.21, pfdr=0.03) and distress from psychotic-like experiences (OR=1.23, pfdr=0.04). Interpretation: Our BD IRS is a novel biological indicator of BD risk. The lack of correlation between the IRS and PRS along with improved MRS prediction suggests the two risk scores capture some orthogonal liability to BD. We show that integrating imaging and genetics is useful for biological characterization of BD and should be considered for the development of clinically relevant prediction models.

items.title: Development and Multicenter Validation of an Ensemble Machine Learning Model for Symptom-Based Triage of Hepatopancreatobiliary Diseases
items.abstract_or_text: Abstract Hepatopancreatobiliary (HPB) diseases are frequently diagnosed late because early symptoms are non-specific and standardized triage tools are limited. We developed and validated a symptom-based machine-learning clinical decision-support model for timely identification and referral of patients at risk of HPB disease. In this ambispective study, 2,296 patients were screened and 2,108 with complete data formed the development cohort; a separate, non-overlapping independent validation cohort of 781 patients (469 HPB-positive and 312 controls) was used for validation. The ensemble model achieved an AUC-ROC of 0.96 (95% CI 0.94–0.98), sensitivity of 76.1%, specificity of 93.9%, accuracy of 83.2%, positive predictive value of 94.9%, negative predictive value of 72.3%, and F1 score of 84.5%. Sensitivity was 14.1 percentage points higher than specialist clinical assessment (76.1% vs 62.0%), corresponding to an approximately 23% relative improvement. A bilingual mobile application enabled real-time symptom-based risk stratification. These findings support further prospective evaluation of the model as a low-cost triage aid, particularly in primary-care and resource-limited settings.

items.title: Academic Integrity in the Age of Artificial Intelligence: A Scoping Review (2026)
items.abstract_or_text: The rapid proliferation of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) and large language models (LLMs) has fundamentally transformed the landscape of modern higher education, prompting a critical paradigm shift in how academic integrity is conceptualized. This scoping review synthesizes 20 cutting-edge academic publications from 2026 (retrieved via Google Scholar) to examine the evolution of academic integrity from mechanical plagiarism detection and punitive surveillance toward comprehensive institutional, pedagogical, and ethical redesign. The synthesis reveals that the primary systemic catalyst for academic misconduct remains the pervasive “publish or perish” culture and quantitative assessment paradigms that prioritize performance over moral growth. Contemporary scholarship moves beyond identifying individual infractions to address systemic vulnerabilities, student uncertainty, data privacy, and the degradation of higher-order cognitive skills (analyzing, evaluating, creating) resulting from unreflective AI reliance. To mitigate these threats, the review highlights four key integrative strategies: (1) adoption of ecosystemic models (e.g., A. Maleki’s Higher Education Integrity Ecosystem) linking governance, assessment, cultural norms, and individual agency; (2) implementation of process-oriented, authentic assessment frameworks (e.g., S. Lehane, A. Wright and P. Fenton’s Model for Practice and P.D.N. Ncube et al.’s PRISMA-based multi-stage evaluations) that render automated cheating obsolete; (3) operationalization of the AI3 model that integrated AI, academic integrity, and assessment innovation (C. DeLuca, L.Volante and M. Holden), and (4) proactive educational initiatives, AI literacy, and epistemic pluralism to safeguard neurodivergent learning trajectories. Ultimately, the academic community is transitioning from technocratic panic to building ethically resilient, adaptive educational ecosystems aligned with UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDG 4 and SDG 16).

items.title: EEG in Parkinson’s Disease: Mechanisms, Biomarkers and Translational Opportunities
items.abstract_or_text: Parkinson’s disease (PD) is characterized by nigrostriatal dopaminergic degeneration and basal ganglia dysfunction, yet these pathophysiological abnormalities alone do not fully explain its heterogeneous motor and non-motor manifestations. Over recent decades, electroencephalography (EEG) has evolved from a primarily descriptive technique into a quantitative approach for investigating cortical electrophysiological dynamics associated with PD. Accumulating electrophysiological evidence implicates altered oscillatory synchronization and interactions across cortical and subcortical circuits in PD-related dysfunction, suggesting disturbances in the temporal coordination of neural activity. Emerging approaches, including large-scale datasets, multimodal integration, individualized modeling and wearable EEG technologies, offer opportunities for physiological phenotyping and real-world monitoring. However, methodological heterogeneity, limited reproducibility, insufficient external validation and uncertainty regarding clinical utility continue to constrain translation. This Review critically synthesizes EEG-derived measures spanning spectral activity, oscillatory coupling, functional connectivity and dynamic brain states, examining their relationships with motor, cognitive and neuropsychiatric manifestations of PD. By distinguishing mechanistic interpretations, clinical associations and current levels of biomarker validation, it identifies opportunities and requirements for translating EEG-derived measures into reliable tools for individualized assessment and clinical decision-making.

items.title: A relational architecture of the human genome
items.abstract_or_text: Complex systems exhibit organization not only through their components but also via their interdependencies. Local nucleotide dependencies underpin regulatory motifs and RNA structures, yet principles governing a higher-order organization across the human genome remain unknown. Here we systematically perturbed every position of the com- plete telomere-to-telomere human genome using Nucleotide Transformer v3 with an ex- ascale compute cluster, generating nucleotide-resolution dependency maps that reveal a directed, weighted network of position-to-position genomic relationships. This network recapitulates known biological features and uncovers recurrent, directional architec- tures termed 'relons', spanning coding, non-coding, and unannotated regions. These re- lational modules reflect evolutionary and functional constraints and associate with hu- man genetic variation and pathogenic variants. Our findings suggest a higher-order rela- tional layer of genome organization, providing a framework to interpret DNA as a complex system of dependencies beyond linear and 3D structure, with implications for under- standing genetic variation and disease.

items.title: Lipid nanoparticle-mediated RNAi targeting of KRAS mutants sensitises colorectal cancer cells to chemotherapy
items.abstract_or_text: KRAS mutations, including G12D, G12V and G13D, are major oncogenic drivers in colorectal cancer (CRC) and are associated with therapeutic resistance. However, approved KRAS inhibitors remain focused on G12C subtype, leaving these prevalent variants without approved targeted therapies. Here, we developed a lipid nanoparticle (LNP)-based RNA interference (RNAi) strategy to target these three KRAS variants using a single small interfering RNA (siRNA) sequence. The developed siRNA-LNPs reduced KRAS mRNA and protein expression in HCT116 (G13D), SW620 (G12V) and LS180 (G12D) cells, but not in KRAS wild-type HT29 cells, suppressing the cellular proliferation, clonogenic survival and migration. Transcriptomic profiling revealed changes in KRAS associated signalling, including suppression of cell-cycle and DNA repair programmes, providing a rationale for combining siRNA silencing with the fluoropyrimidine chemotherapeutic agent 5-fluorouracil (5-FU). The combination produced synergistic effects across all three KRAS-mutant CRC cell models and enhanced the apoptosis in both monolayer cultures and 3D spheroids. Collectively, these findings provide proof of concept for this combination strategy and support its further investigation as a potential therapeutic approach for KRAS-mutant CRC.

items.title: THE BILE ACID RECEPTOR TGR5 MODULATES HIPPOCAMPAL NEURAL STEM CELL STATE AND AGEING
items.abstract_or_text: Ageing locks hippocampal neural stem cells (NSCs) into deeper quiescence and inflammation-driven senescence, which are also associated with impaired cognition. The bile-acid receptor TGR5, a member class I G-protein coupled receptors (GPCRs), is expressed in cultured hippocampal NSCs and in SOX2-positive cells of the adult sub granular zone, yet its role in NSC homeostasis is unknown. In this study we show that TGR5 selective agonist, TC-G 1005, expanded the NSC pool without forcing neuronal differentiation. Primary NSCs treatment with TC-G 1005 increased BrdU incorporation and PCNA in a concentration-dependent manner, and both responses were lost after TGR5 knockdown. TGR5 agonism in differentiating cultures increased nestin, left doublecortin (DCX) unchanged and suppressed MAP2 expression, preserving stemness rather than neuronal commitment. The agonist also released BMP4-imposed quiescence, lowering FOXO3a and restoring phospho-EGFR and ASCL1, and reopened autophagic flux, with less p62 and LC3-II, fewer LAMP2 puncta and more Beclin-1. Furthermore, activation of TGR5 suppressed IL-6 induced p53 and p16 expression, restored proliferation and contracted the inflammatory transcriptome by more than 90%, including Cdkn2a, Cdkn2b and Cdk6. In 18-month-old mice, brain-penetrant TC-G 1005 (5 mg/kg, subcutaneously, twice daily for 28 days) expanded SOX2-positive and proliferating NSCs, reduced p16, recovered ASCL1 and improved spatial memory, without changing locomotion or generating DCX-positive neurons. Dentate gyrus-restricted TGR5 knockdown abolished these cellular effects and the rescue of spatial and social discrimination. Hippocampal proteomic analysis revealed that TC-G 1005 treated aged mice occupied an intermediate, partially rejuvenated position between young and aged proteomes, with 86 proteins shared between ageing- and treatment-responsive sets, and mitochondrial and complement C1q modules shifted toward youthful levels. TGR5 activation therefore relieves both quiescence and senescence in the aged neurogenic niche without driving neuronal differentiation. Collectively, these results suggest that TGR5 could be targeted to preserve cognition in ageing by rejuvenating the hippocampal stem-cell niche.

items.title: Synthetic Aperture Radar, Multi-Source Data Fusion, and Machine Learning for Aboveground Biomass and Carbon Stock Estimation: A Systematic Review and Bibliometric Analysis
items.abstract_or_text: Abstract Accurate estimation of aboveground biomass (AGB) and carbon stocks is fundamental for sustainable forest management, climate change mitigation, and ecosystem monitoring. Advances in synthetic aperture radar (SAR), multi-source remote sensing, and artificial intelligence have substantially improved biomass estimation; however, existing research remains methodologically fragmented, with limited synthesis of sensor fusion strategies, machine learning, and deep learning approaches, and their applicability to urban tree carbon estimation. This study presents a systematic review and bibliometric analysis of peer-reviewed literature published between 2004 and 2026 following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA 2020) guidelines. Literature was retrieved from Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar, screened using Rayyan, and 68 eligible studies were identified for qualitative synthesis. The review examined publication trends, geographical distribution, remote sensing platforms, data fusion strategies, machine learning and deep learning algorithms, validation approaches, and emerging research gaps. The findings reveal a substantial increase in publications after 2018, driven by the widespread availability of Sentinel-1, Sentinel-2, LiDAR, cloud-based geospatial platforms, and advances in artificial intelligence. The reviewed literature demonstrates a clear transition from single-sensor approaches towards feature-level fusion of SAR, optical, and LiDAR data, which consistently improved biomass and carbon estimation compared with individual sensors. Among predictive models, ensemble learning algorithms, particularly Random Forest and Extreme Gradient Boosting, remained the most robust and widely adopted, while deep learning approaches showed increasing potential for high-resolution applications where sufficient training data were available. Despite these advances, research focusing specifically on urban tree biomass and carbon estimation remains limited, highlighting challenges related to heterogeneous urban environments, limited reference datasets, SAR integration, and model transferability. This review provides a comprehensive synthesis of current methodological developments, identifies critical knowledge gaps, and proposes future research directions to develop robust, scalable, interpretable, and transferable frameworks for biomass and carbon estimation across natural and urban ecosystems.

items.title: scMTG reconstructs single-cell temporal dynamics with Markov transition generators
items.abstract_or_text: Single-cell time-series data offer a unique opportunity to study how cell states emerge, evolve, and diversify over time. However, cells are destructively measured across time points and individual cells cannot be directly tracked, making it challenging to reconstruct cell-state transitions and uncover the dynamic regulatory programs. Existing methods are predominantly based on optimal transport and typically require predefined low-dimensional representations, which can limit scalability, flexibility, and mechanistic interpretability. Here we present scMTG, a single-cell Markov transition generative framework that jointly learns cell representations and temporal cell-state transitions from unpaired single-cell time-series data. In a series of experiments, scMTG demonstrates superior performance in interpolating held-out missing-time-point data and inferring cross-time-point transition matrices, compared with state-of-the-art methods. More importantly, the learned Markov transition generator provides an interpretable framework for identifying the molecular programs that drive cell-state changes, enabling characterization of cell fate decisions and construction of time-resolved regulatory networks. Together, scMTG provides a unified generative framework for reconstructing cellular dynamics and uncovering regulatory programs that shape development, differentiation, and disease progression. scMTG is available as open-source software at https://github.com/liuq-lab/scMTG.

items.title: Rapid, reversible RNA/DNA precipitation using rare earth ion coordination
items.abstract_or_text: Efficient recovery and removal of nucleic acids remain major challenges in molecular biology, diagnostics, and viral-vector manufacturing. Conventional precipitation methods often require organic solvents, low temperatures, and extended centrifugation, while nuclease-based contaminant removal can be incomplete and/or is incompatible with downstream workflows. Here, we evaluate NADA, a trivalent rare earth-based reagent, for rapid, solvent-free precipitation of RNA and DNA, and ALGO-mediated recovery of the full range of properties of unmodified RNA. Using hepatitis B virus pre-genomic RNA, lambda bacteriophage DNA, and the HBV nucleocapsid as model systems, we show that NADA rapidly sequesters both ssRNA and dsDNA from solution, reducing Midori Green nucleic acid fluorescence and UV absorption to baseline levels. The NADA complex prevents HBV core protein binding to the HBV pgRNA, and therefore triggering of nucleocapsid formation, even when added simultaneously with core protein, suggesting that lanthanide ion coordination, out-competes the cognate Cp for viral RNA-binding interactions. Recovery with ALGO restores pgRNA integrity and functionality, enabling subsequent assembly of the expected T=4/T=3 nucleocapsids. In contrast, pre-assembled nucleocapsids resist NADA-ALGO treatment, demonstrating coat protein capsid-mediated protection of encapsidated pgRNA. Similar outcomes for lambda dsDNA establish NADA/ALGO as a rapid, reversible, and selective alternative platform for nucleic acid precipitation, with potential applications in viral particle purification, contaminant removal, and RNA handling workflows.

items.title: High-plex protein imaging across thick tissue by synchronized amplification
items.abstract_or_text: High-plex protein imaging is essential for decoding complex tissue organization, yet it remains largely confined to thin sections. Current approaches in millimeter-thick samples suffer from poor signal penetration and depth-dependent, uneven signal amplification. Even with specialized instrumentation to facilitate probe diffusion, iterative millimeter-thick tissue workflows can take more than four days per staining round, and reported eleven-marker experiments extend beyond a month. We introduce Amplification by Cyclic Extension (ACE), a DNA-barcoded, synchronized in situ amplification strategy that uses thermally controlled cyclic extension to coordinate DNA concatemer growth across tissue depths. By synchronously activating and coordinating reaction progression throughout the sample, ACE enables controlled, uniform signal amplification across tissue depths. Using ACE, we demonstrate 63-plex protein and RNA imaging in thin sections, 22-plex protein imaging in 200 μm mouse brain sections, and 16-plex protein imaging in 1 mm-thick brain tissue encompassing over three million cells. For millimeter-thick tissues, ACE reduces per-round target-switching time from multiple days to less than eight hours, shifting volumetric high-plex protein imaging from months to days. Together, these results establish ACE as a synchronized amplification strategy that enables scalable high-plex protein imaging in thick tissues.

items.title: Foundation Model Artificial Intelligence for Electrocardiogram Detection of Rheumatic Mitral Stenosis
items.abstract_or_text: Background: Rheumatic mitral stenosis (RMS) disproportionately affects low-resource settings where echocardiography is limited. We evaluated foundation model (FM) feasibility for RMS detection using limited, indirectly labeled ECGs. Methods: An ECG-FM was fine-tuned using 804 RMS-positive ECGs per fold and externally validated across clinical and wearable lead configurations. Results: Internal AUROCs were 0.89, 0.87, and 0.87, for 12-Lead, 6-Lead, and 1-Lead respectively. External AUROCs were 0.82, 0.80, and 0.77. Performance remained comparable across demographic subgroups. Conclusions: FM fine-tuning enables RMS detection using limited ICD-derived labels, supporting further evaluation of reduced-lead ECG screening and echocardiography triage in resource-constrained settings.

items.title: BanglaDiaHallu: Hallucinations of large language models and the effect of guideline-grounded retrieval-augmented generation in Bangla diabetes question answering
items.abstract_or_text: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly consulted for health advice, but they can produce fluent statements that are false or unsupported, known as hallucinations, and this risk is poorly characterised in low-resource languages such as Bangla. We measured hallucinations of locally deployable open-weight LLMs in Bangla diabetes question answering and tested whether retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) grounded in Bangladeshs National Guideline on Diabetes Mellitus reduces them. Forty patient questions spanning six clinical sub-domains were each answered twice, under zero-shot prompting, by Qwen3.5-9B, TigerLLM-9B, Qwen3.6-35B-A3B and Gemma-4-26B-A4B, and by BanglaDiaRAG, which adds hybrid dense (BGE-M3) and sparse (BM25) retrieval from a physician-reviewed Bangla guideline knowledge base to Qwen3.5-9B. Two physicians rated the 400 de-identified responses by consensus for medical accuracy, completeness, safety, readability and reliability on a 0-1 scale, and responses with accuracy below 0.70 were classified as hallucinated. Hallucination rates were 2.5% for Gemma-4-26B-A4B, 3.8% for TigerLLM-9B, 22.5% for Qwen3.6-35B-A3B and 77.5% for Qwen3.5-9B. Guideline grounding lowered the rate of Qwen3.5-9B to 11.3% (difference -66.3 percentage points; 95% CI -76.3 to -55.0) and raised every criterion by 0.24 to 0.38 points (Holm-adjusted p < 0.001). BanglaDiaRAG outscored Qwen3.6-35B-A3B on all five criteria and matched or exceeded TigerLLM-9B, but it remained below Gemma-4-26B-A4B in safety, readability and reliability, and its residual errors were specific, confident and potentially harmful. Guideline grounding can turn a weak general-purpose model into a much safer Bangla diabetes assistant, but the choice of base model mattered as much as retrieval and no configuration was free of hallucination, so clinical oversight remains essential before patient-facing use.

items.title: Diagnostic accuracy of deep learning for microsatellite instability prediction in gastric cancer: A systematic review and meta-analysis
items.abstract_or_text: Deep learning (DL) applied to haematoxylin and eosin (H&E)-stained pathology images can predict microsatellite instability (MSI) in gastric cancer (GC). We evaluated its diagnostic accuracy and discriminative performance. PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library and Web of Science were searched for studies applying DL to H&E images for MSI prediction in GC. The protocol was prospectively registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261503140). Risk of bias was assessed with QUADAS-2. Pooled sensitivity and specificity were estimated with a bivariate random-effects model, with subgroup analyses by validation strategy and data source; slide-level areas under the curve (AUCs) were pooled after logit transformation. Prespecified scenario analyses assessed robustness. Ten studies were included; seven independent datasets from six studies entered the primary synthesis. Pooled sensitivity, specificity and summary receiver operating characteristic AUC were 0.78 (95% CI 0.63-0.88), 0.85 (95% CI 0.77-0.90) and 0.89 (95% CI 0.86-0.91); nine studies contributed to the secondary AUC synthesis (pooled AUC 0.85, 95% CI 0.80-0.89). Hospital-derived cohorts showed numerically higher sensitivity (0.86) and diagnostic odds ratio (39.8) than TCGA-derived cohorts (0.71 and 11.5), but subgroup differences were limited by the small number of studies and substantial heterogeneity. DL models show good diagnostic accuracy for MSI prediction in GC, but clinical utility still requires confirmation in standardised multicentre, independent external and prospective studies.

items.title: The Ability of Generative Artificial Intelligence to Evaluate the Quality of Scholarly Output
items.abstract_or_text: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly being considered as tools to support the peer-review process. However, we currently have a limited understanding of their capabilities and biases in this area. In a set of three studies, we examined how out-of-the box LLMs evaluate scientific quality when presented with controlled, systematically manipulated research abstracts from various scientific disciplines (Study 1 & 2), and psychological science in particular (Study 3). Our design independently varied six key dimensions: Novelty, Analysis Quality, Internal Validity, Sample Size, Preregistration, and Statistical Significance. The results showed that GPT-4o-mini is sensitive to all six variables to some extent, but Statistical Significance had by far the strongest effect: Abstracts that mentioned finding a statistically significant effect received substantially higher ratings compared to abstracts that reported null effects but were otherwise identical. In contrast, newer models with more reasoning capabilities (i.e., GPT-5.6-terra and Claude-sonnet-5) consistently preferred abstracts with higher sample size, analysis quality and internal validity. Abstracts mentioning that the study was preregistered also tended to receive somewhat higher ratings. Interestingly, statistical significance and novelty consistently failed to explain a significant amount of variability in the ratings of those models. Taken together, these results highlight both the potential of advanced LLMs to support scientific evaluation and the importance of understanding the criteria that drive their judgments before incorporating them into peer-review workflows.

items.title: Preemptive SOD1 Silencing via Neonatal Intramuscular AAV Therapy Modifies Disease Trajectory in an ALS Mouse Model
items.abstract_or_text: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) is a progressive and fatal neurodegenerative disorder with limited therapeutic options. Mutations in the gene encoding superoxide dismutase 1 (SOD1) represent a major genetic cause of familial ALS, driving motor neuron degeneration through toxic gain-of-function mechanisms. Although gene silencing approaches targeting SOD1 show substantial therapeutic potential, their clinical translation remains restricted by suboptimal delivery to the spinal motor neurons and safety concerns linked to conventional viral vectors. This study presents a minimally invasive gene therapy strategy that combines the retrograde transport capability of rAAV2-retro with the safety of an artificial microRNA (miRNA) to achieve pan-spinal SOD1 silencing. A single intramuscular injection of rAAV2-retro-miRNA into neonatal SOD1G93A mice resulted in widespread transduction of spinal motor neurons, significant reduction of mutant SOD1 protein, and multifaceted therapeutic benefits. Treated mice exhibited delayed disease onset, extended lifespan, preserved motor function, reduced neuroinflammation, and protection of neuromuscular junctions and spinal motor neurons. Importantly, the artificial miRNA construct demonstrated a superior safety profile relative to short hairpin RNA (shRNA)-based constructs, which induced marked toxicity and lethality in wild-type mice. These findings establish neonatal intramuscular delivery of rAAV2-retro-miRNA as a safe, efficient, and clinically translatable strategy for preemptive intervention in SOD1-mediated ALS, offering broader applicability to other motor neuron diseases.

items.title: Network-enabled drug repurposing identifies lithium to promote cardiomyocyte proliferation
items.abstract_or_text: The adult mammalian heart has minimal regenerative capacity, limited in part by endogenous cardiomyocyte (CM) renewal. Although CM proliferation is a promising target in both congenital and adult heart disease, no current therapies specifically target this process. Progress has been hindered by the complexity of CM proliferation signaling networks, which may require systems-level approaches. The overall goal of this study was to leverage systems modeling to identify FDA approved drugs that have the potential to be repurposed towards CM proliferation. To achieve this goal, we developed a computational drug repurposing framework that integrates drug-target interaction data with a previously developed logic-based network model of CM proliferation signaling. Using this framework, we identified 81 drugs that directly target nodes within the CM proliferation network, corresponding to 32 unique drug-target interactions. Virtual screening predicted 5 unique drug-target interactions that increase CM proliferation and 14 that decrease CM proliferation outputs. Lithium, a GSK3{beta} inhibitor widely prescribed for bipolar disorder, was predicted and experimentally validated to promote CM proliferation through a Cyclin D/CDK4 pathway. In vivo, treatment of pregnant mice with lithium increased DNA synthesis in the CMs of their embryos. A retrospective analysis of the FDA Adverse Events Reporting System confirmed that relative to other mood stabilizers, in utero exposure to lithium was associated with an increased incidence of congenital heart defects, in males but not females. Together, this work provides a computational-experimental framework for repurposing FDA-approved drugs to modulate CM proliferation, which highlights therapeutic potential of lithium for adult CM regeneration but congenital risks to developing embryos.
